rows.title: Review of the formerly unreviewed R6a Bullet Optimizer rows
rows.summary: Now: every R6a optimizer verdict holds, with no code change. The statement box is 16 px on touch screens (pointer-coarse:text-base, DPH-30/36). The optimizer is the kit Dialog, size lg, full screen below sm (max-sm:h-dvh, overlay max-sm:p-0) with the body as the only scroll region (DPH-37, DVIS-07). The footer wraps, uses kit buttons and keeps Copy at the start (DPH-38). The quality tiles stack below 640 px (grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3, DPH-41/43). The power-verb row and its categories wrap, with no 280 px cap and no sideways scroll (DPH-42). The Dialog's own portal keeps the optimizer out of a faded hidden entry (DVIS-23). Fail-first run 36518113356 is green for 8e97533, e3b2030, d529431 and e4cc82f.
rows.product_call: Two earlier claims were overtaken on purpose. DVIS-07's 'Escape closes even after a rewrite' is reversed by R5-OPT-01. DVIS-23's outer Portal (5f52d43) was removed in 56e42bf because the Dialog's own portal does the same job.
rows.remaining: DPH-30/36/37/38 and DVIS-07 stay partial in the tracker only for their non-optimizer dialogs (Cover Letter Generator, Header Icon picker, NewLetter, ShareLink), which belong to the dlg cluster. 5f52d43 alone cannot be re-proven, as its code is gone; the DVIS-23 test is proven against e3b2030 (runs 36453755199, 36518113356).

rows.title: STAR Optimizer → Use Template replaces the edited statement with no way back
rows.summary: Now: after a template replaces the statement, 'Restore my statement' stays through typing, Auto-Fix, the chips and further template picks, and brings back the user's own statement. It goes once used, or once the text is that statement again. 102-r4-dux-22-template-undo's old 'Undo gone after an edit' assertion was reversed to this intended behaviour, and it now asserts more.
rows.product_call: The restore link keeps the statement from before the first template of this session, not the last edit.

rows.title: Escape in the optimizer throws away a rewritten statement
rows.summary: Now: Escape closes the optimizer only while the statement is unchanged. After a rewrite it is ignored, and that ignored Escape stops at the optimizer, so an issue dialog around the editor stays open too. This is unchanged by claude/r4-green's inert closing Dialog panel, as the optimizer is unmounted on close and close() does nothing once open is false (clean merge, git merge-tree).
rows.product_call: A rewritten statement is closed only with Cancel or Apply, never by a stray Escape.
rows.remaining: No feedback is given when Escape is ignored (noted as a11y, deferred).

rows.title: Body text after a list (a blockquote) joins the last ATS bullet
rows.summary:
Now: a quote or
after a list stays apart from the last bullet everywhere, including after the description is edited. The ATS ends the open bullet at a block outside every list (6d9ac2a). The editor's sanitizer, which the next edit saves, now closes the list before such a block instead of putting it into the last
  • as a

    . Before, one typed character glued the quote back onto the bullet. The Markdown export prints it as a paragraph of its own, not as the item's continuation (af15d53). A quote or paragraph inside an item still stays in it.
rows.product_call: An ATS bullet is a list item plus what is inside that item. Body text outside the list is never part of a bullet. In the PDF and Word a quote prints as an indented paragraph of its own (paragraph gap, no marker), the same column a paragraph inside a level-1 item has; that look is left as it is.
rows.remaining:
The sanitizer still stores a top-level
as a plain

(its indent is lost on save). This is older behaviour for every quote, not only after a list, and is left as it is.

rows.title: Text after a nested list opens as its own line in the optimizer but joins the outer item in the ATS
rows.summary:
Now: the optimizer opens a list item's whole statement across a nested list, as the ATS scores it. Apply rewrites that statement, keeps the sub-list and leaves no
or empty paragraph. The Playwright spec pins the saved HTML in Chromium.
rows.product_call: The statement the optimizer edits is the one the ATS scores: an item's own text before and after its nested list.
rows.remaining: The Playwright spec cannot be proven fail-first (failfirst runs node only); its real-browser evidence is red run 36460322150 on 058d471, then green on 9d40631 and in full gate 36463569183. The node tests for 058d471 and 9d40631 rely on the test's own imitation of Chrome's delete.

rows.title: The ATS and optimizer weak-phrase lists differ; a power-verb chip on a negative statement
rows.summary: Now: the ATS score and the optimizer read one weak-phrase list (WEAK_PHRASE_REPLACEMENTS), and every phrase has an Auto-Fix. A power-verb chip leaves a statement that opens with a helper verb or a negative unchanged and shows a rewrite tip: Did not, Was, Never, Could not, Can't, Won't, and now also No, Nobody, None, Nothing, Neither, Nor and Zero (5ceb67c). Before, 'No customer data was lost' read 'Spearheaded no customer data was lost'. 'No-code …' and 'Zero-downtime …' still take a verb. The chip keeps 'efforts to' after 'Led'.
rows.product_call: A chip never puts a verb in front of a negative statement; the user rewrites it as something they did. A hyphenated noun that starts with No or Zero is not a negative.
rows.remaining: The negatives part was committed under the ID R4-SW-WT-04; it is this scope item. f849efd changes a test title only.

issues.resolution: confirmed by reading sanitizeRichText and markdownBody; fixed in af15d53 (test corrected in 89119f0); fail-first 36519427309 green, named tests 36519429796 and 36519166141 green apart from the corrected assertion

issues.issue: R4-SW-WT-03 (low): 'No customer data was lost' took the chip's verb ('Spearheaded no customer data…'); No/Nobody/Neither/Zero were not in AUXILIARY_LEAD
issues.resolution: confirmed by reading insertActionVerb (no/nobody/neither/zero match no rule before the verb is prepended); fixed in 5ceb67c; fail-first job in 36519147360 green, named tests 36519166141 green for it

rejected.reason: The finding says the PDF prints a quote after a list at the item's text column, like an in-item paragraph. True, but it is layout, not a scoring error: the PDF and Word print a quote as its own indented paragraph wherever it is, and Word uses the same column for both too. The data bug (the sanitizer) and the Markdown export are fixed; the PDF look is left as it is and recorded as a product call.

d529431: the quality tiles are grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3, so they stack below 640 px (DPH-43 is its duplicate). 103-r4-dph-41-quality-tiles, run 36518113356.

notes: Two reviewer findings were confirmed and fixed (af15d53 + 89119f0 for SW-WT-01, 5ceb67c for SW-WT-03). Every fix commit has a green fail-first run. Named tests over every file that uses richText, markdownExport, atsChecker or bulletOptimizer ran in 36519166141 (958/961 pass, the one failure the wrong <dt> expectation fixed in 89119f0; lint green) and 36519429796 (green). The last full gate is 36463569183 on 9d40631 (suite 6/6, Playwright 3/3, Cypress 4/4, build, lint); the full gate has not been re-run on this head, so the coordinator's batch gate should cover af15d53 and 5ceb67c.
